title.en: Magnetic field of a current loop

summary: Build a field around a real conductor path and keep the on-axis analytic result distinct from off-axis numerical sampling.
objective: Build a current loop whose on-axis field follows the analytic expression while off-axis probes are labelled as numerical samples.
intent_signals: Show the magnetic field around a loop of current.
Compare the field at the centre of a loop with the field along its axis.
example_prompts: Build a current loop with an axial field readout and probe points along the axis.
Stack loops into a short solenoid and show the field between them.
negative_signals: Not a full electromagnetic solver: no time variation, induced currents or materials.
Not a magnet design tool; no saturation, cores or losses.
not_for: Not a full electromagnetic solver: no time variation, induced currents or materials.
Not a magnet design tool; no saturation, cores or losses.

entities.name: Conductor path
entities.guidance: Model the loop as a real conductor with a direction marker, since the field direction follows the current sense.

entities.name: Axial probes
entities.guidance: Place probes along the axis where the analytic expression applies and label their values as analytic.

entities.name: Off-axis sampling
entities.guidance: Use the stated periodic midpoint Biot-Savart quadrature, compare N with 2N and label the difference a refinement diagnostic rather than a certified error estimate. Exclude the stated neighborhood of every ideal filament.

state_contract.model: One or more coaxial circular ideal filaments of finite positive radius R, signed current I and axial offset z0. Each loop contributes axial Bz=mu0 I R^2/[2(R^2+(z-z0)^2)^(3/2)]. Off-axis evaluation uses a periodic midpoint quadrature with N=256 uniformly spaced conductor angles by default and a comparison against 2N; the difference is a refinement diagnostic, not a certified error bound. At angle phi use x=(R cos(phi),R sin(phi),z0), dl=(-R sin(phi),R cos(phi),0)dphi and dB=mu0 I dl cross (p-x)/(4 pi |p-x|^3). Reject probes within the chosen exclusion radius 0.02R of any filament, and label that radius as a numerical/display policy. Sum all loop contributions; at zero total field draw no direction. Wire thickness is display geometry only.
state_contract.authority: Loop radii, axial offsets and signed currents are authoritative; readouts and arrows derive from their superposition.
actions: Change the current or the loop radius.
Move an axial probe and read the analytic value.
Add loops to form a short solenoid.

invariants: Reversing every loop current reverses the total field; changing just one loop recomputes the superposition. A zero vector has no direction.

For one loop, its own axial centre contribution equals the single-loop centre formula; for multiple loops every axial readout equals the sum of each shifted loop contribution, not the single-loop expression.
Off-axis arrows are labelled as numerical samples and state their sample count.
motion_guidance: Animate current flow along the conductor as a moving marker to convey direction, not as an energy or speed claim.

Update field arrows continuously while a parameter changes; the on-axis magnitude follows the stated expression, which falls off as the inverse cube of distance far from the loop and is finite at the centre, so no single inverse-distance rule is implied.
known_limits: Steady currents in thin conductors; no time-dependent fields, induction or magnetic materials.
Off-axis fidelity depends on quadrature, finite precision and probe distance from the ideal filament; refinement differences are diagnostics, not measured accuracy.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: On the axis of a circular current loop of radius R the magnetic field magnitude is mu-zero times current times R squared divided by twice the quantity axial distance squared plus R squared raised to the power three halves, which reduces at the centre to mu-zero times current divided by twice R.
claims.scope: Steady current in a thin circular loop, on-axis points only, as cited.

source_refs.locator: 12.4, on-axis field expression and centre value

claims.statement: The Biot-Savart law gives the differential field contribution of a current element as mu-zero over four pi times I dl cross the unit vector to the field point divided by the square of the distance, and the field of a finite length of current-carrying wire is found by integrating that expression along the wire.
claims.scope: Steady currents in thin conductors; the idealised filament expression is singular on the wire itself, which is why the scene excludes a neighbourhood of the conductor from numerical sampling.

source_refs.locator: 12.1, differential contribution and integration along the wire

object_craft.structure: A torus-section conductor with visible thickness, terminals and a current direction arrow following the wire. That thickness is display geometry only: the field model treats the conductor as an idealised filament, not as a finite cross-section current distribution.
object_craft.material: Conductive metal family with a distinct terminal material; keep the wire dark enough that field arrows remain legible.
object_craft.articulation: A travelling marker indicates current direction; the conductor itself is static.

object_craft.structure: Probe markers on a rail along the axis with numeric plates and a shared scale legend for arrow length.
object_craft.material: Analytic and numerical values use distinct plate styles so their provenance is visible at a glance.
object_craft.articulation: Probes slide along the axis and recompute continuously.

physical_contract.scope: Static field evaluation and presentation; no dynamics, induction or material response.
checks: For a single loop the centre value matches the analytic expression within tolerance; once further loops are added the single-loop centre expression no longer describes the total field, which is reported as a superposition.
Reversing all loop currents negates every nonzero total vector; zero vectors remain zero with no arrow.
